summary: The Marshall Islands' Division of Immigration lists US, Palauan and Micronesian citizens as visa-exempt with no period restrictions; waives visas for 90 days (in any 180-day period) for EU member countries and the United Kingdom, and for 90 days for Taiwan and Guatemala; gives a 90-day visa on arrival, fee waived, to citizens of the countries on its list of those with diplomatic relations or Pacific Islands Forum membership; and says all other nationalities must obtain a visa before travelling, with a USD 100 non-refundable fee for the Visitor's Visa.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for the Marshall Islands?
faq.answer: US citizens do not: the Division of Immigration says that under the Compact of Free Association US citizens are fully exempt from visa requirements, and its list gives them, and citizens of Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia, no period restrictions. EU member countries and the United Kingdom get a visa waiver for 90 days in any 180-day period, and Taiwan and Guatemala for 90 days; citizens of countries with diplomatic relations with the Marshall Islands, including Pacific Islands Forum members, Australia, New Zealand, Canada, Japan and South Korea, are eligible for a visa on arrival or visa waiver. All other nationalities must obtain a visa before travelling; the Visitor's Visa fee is USD 100, non-refundable.

faq.question: How does the visa on arrival work?
faq.answer: The Division of Immigration's list gives citizens of the countries on its visa-on-arrival list 90 days from the date of arrival, with the fee waived. Everyone entering on a visa on arrival must hold a passport valid for at least 6 months from the intended date of departure, a confirmed return or onward ticket, any visa needed for the onward destination, and sufficient funds for the stay. Extensions, change of status, employment, study and research are not permitted.

faq.question: How long can I stay in the Marshall Islands?
faq.answer: Up to 90 days under the visa waiver or the visa on arrival. For EU and UK citizens extensions, change of status and employment are not permitted; for Taiwanese and Guatemalan passport holders and visa-on-arrival holders, study is excluded as well. US citizens, and citizens of Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia, have no period restrictions.

faq.question: Can Americans work in the Marshall Islands under the Compact?
faq.answer: Not on the Compact alone. The RMI Division of Immigration says that under the Compact US citizens enjoy specific exemptions regarding RMI entry visas, though work registration is still required.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory?
faq.answer: No official source we could read makes travel insurance a condition of entry. The UK government says medical facilities are very limited and to make sure you have comprehensive travel insurance which covers all medical costs, including medical evacuation.

entryRequirements.vaccinations.yellow-fe.text: Cholera and Yellow Fever immunizations are required for those arriving from infected areas.

entryRequirements.vaccinations.mmr-child.text: All Incoming Travellers to RMI & domestic travel to neighbouring islands – Effective immediately- (MANDATORY) • All children less than 5 years must have their vaccinations for MMR (or Measles and Rubella) up-to date. This includes immunization for infants aged between 6 months and 11 months. This is called a “zero dose”
Proof of vaccination must be presented upon entry into the RMI or entry may be denied (entry can be granted with an undertaking to receive these vaccinations within 48 hours of arrival).
Only a physicians recommendation will be accepted for exemptions to receiving the MMR vaccine.

entryRequirements.travelInsurance.text: Medical facilities are very limited. Make sure you have comprehensive travel insurance which covers all medical costs, including medical evacuation. Bring sufficient supplies of prescription medicines with you.

entryRequirements.declarations.arrival-c.text: You must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.
You must declare cash in any currency worth more than 10,000 US dollars.

countryFacts.safety.text: Crime rates are low in the Marshall Islands, but there is a risk of petty crime, including break-ins and non-violent theft.
The crime rate is low, but assaults and petty crimes, such as break-ins and theft occur.
Be alert for feral dogs which are common and can attack.
Travelling by boat, especially on open waters between atolls, can be hazardous.

entryRequirements.overstay.text: §147. Holder of visa or permit not to remain in the Republic after expiry. Every person to whom a visa or permit is granted under this Chapter or under the Labor (Non-Resident Workers) Act 2006 and who is in the Republic after the expiry of that visa or permit, shall deemed to be in the Republic unlawfully.

§148. Liability for removal (1) Any person who is in the Republic unlawfully pursuant to Section 147 of this Chapter , may be the subject of a removal order provided that: Immigration Act 2006 43MIRC Ch.1§149 l Page31 (a) the person has been unlawfully in the Republic: (i) for a period of more than 14 consecutive days after the expiry of that visa or permit;

§173. Unlawfully being in the Republic. Any person found to be unlawfully in the Republic pursuant to section 147, and any other applicable section of the Act, is guilty of an offence and is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 5 years, a fine not exceeding $10,000 or both.
(2) Any person that has been deported or removed from the Republic under this Chapter shall not be allowed to re-enter the Republic.
